abstracts.abstract: This paper introduces a novel theoretical framework for understanding the convergence behavior of adaptive metaheuristics in large-scale combinatorial optimization problems. Unlike traditional analysis approaches that rely on Markov chain theory or asymptotic convergence proofs, we develop a dynamical systems perspective that characterizes algorithm trajectories through attractor basins in high-dimensional solution spaces. We establish fundamental connections between problem structure, characterized by ruggedness measures and fitness landscape topology, and algorithmic behavior under this new paradigm. Our main theoretical contribution proves that adaptive operators exhibiting history-dependent transition probabilities converge to stable solution distributions determined by landscape-induced potential functions. This finding challenges the conventional wisdom that metaheuristic performance is primarily determined by operator design, revealing instead that landscape-structure alignment governs achievable solution quality. We further demonstrate that this framework generates testable predictions verified through extensive computational experiments on structured benchmark instances. The proposed paradigm shift enables rigorous analysis of when and why heuristic search methods succeed or fail, providing theoretical foundations previously absent in the metaheuristics literature. Our work opens new research directions connecting statistical physics of disordered systems with operations research algorithm design.

We present refined theoretical analysis of branch-and-bound algorithms for integer programming that significantly tightens existing complexity bounds. Previous work established that worst-case performance for general integer programs is exponential, yet such bounds fail to capture practical behavior on structured instances. Our analysis introduces a novel measure termed solution density that characterizes how integer feasible points distribute within the LP relaxation polyhedron. We prove that when solution density exceeds a computable threshold, the algorithm exhibits dramatically improved performance bounds: from exponential to pseudopolynomial in the problem dimension. For the specific case of mixed-integer sets arising from network flow problems, we derive explicit complexity formulas showing dependence on graph-theoretic parameters including treewidth and cycle rank. These results explain empirically observed efficiency of modern MILP solvers on network-structured instances and provide theoretical justification for preprocessing techniques that exploit sparsity. Additionally, we establish new cutting plane separation results for the knapsack polytope, demonstrating that gap-closing cuts can be generated in time polynomial in the number of variables when the profit-to-weight ratios satisfy a bounded range condition. Computational experiments on benchmark instances confirm that our theoretical predictions accurately estimate actual solver performance, enabling instance-specific algorithm selection strategies.

We introduce an integrated decision support architecture that unifies constraint programming, metaheuristic search, and machine learning for real-time scheduling under uncertainty. Traditional approaches treat these components as separate modules, requiring ad-hoc coordination that fails to exploit synergies. Our system, termed Adaptive Optimization Network (AON), embeds a learned cost model within a constraint programming framework, enabling dynamic operator selection during search based on predicted solution quality and feasibility probability. The architecture employs a novel bi-level optimization structure where upper-level reinforcement learning agents adjust search strategies while lower-level constraint programming solvers execute neighborhood exploration. We demonstrate that this tight integration enables the system to adaptively switch between exact propagation and heuristic diversification based on runtime performance metrics. For stochastic optimization scenarios involving uncertain processing times and resource availability, AON maintains probability distributions over constraints that are dynamically refined as scenarios are explored. A key innovation is the explanation module that provides interpretable justifications for schedule modifications, supporting human decision-makers in high-stakes manufacturing environments. Computational evaluation on benchmark scheduling instances and a real-world semiconductor manufacturing case demonstrates superior performance compared to state-of-the-art approaches, with solution quality improvements of 15-30% on tardiness minimization problems.

This paper presents significant enhancements to large-scale simulation optimization systems through a hybrid parallelization framework exploiting heterogeneous computing resources. Existing simulation-based optimization approaches suffer from poor scalability when applied to complex stochastic systems with expensive function evaluations. Our system introduces a three-tier parallelization architecture: coarse-grained parallelism across multiple simulation replications, medium-grained parallelism within simulation runs through discrete-event decomposition, and fine-grained parallelism using GPU-accelerated random number generation and statistical estimation. A novel adaptive allocation algorithm dynamically redistributes computational resources between exploration and exploitation phases based on estimated solution surface curvature and variance characteristics. We develop an enhanced metamodel-assisted optimization module that combines Gaussian process surrogates with local search, incorporating heteroscedastic error modeling to properly weight simulation observations of varying reliability. For problems involving rare events or tail probability estimation, we implement importance sampling schemes that adapt based on gradient information from the metamodel. The system includes an automated experimental design component that minimizes simulation budget while maximizing information gain. Implementation details and software architecture are provided to enable reproducibility. Extensive computational experiments on inventory management, queueing network, and healthcare scheduling problems demonstrate 5-8x speedup over previous state-of-the-art systems while maintaining solution quality, enabling practical application to previously intractable problem sizes.
